crime: At ten, {WITCH_NAME} read her notebook aloud, telling where every old thing in the house had come from. Without looking up from his plate, her father asked, "Who are you telling this to?" She shut the notebook and never opened it again. After that, when her Magic made a broken thing answer, she asked it only which part was failing, never what it had been through.

In the prison, another girl streamed from her phone in the lounge every evening of free time so the nights would not be so quiet, and she gave the last half hour to {WITCH_NAME}, whose Magic set an old thing telling its story. One night, her hair still wet, the streamer said, "I've never heard one. That's my shower time. Nobody's asking, so tomorrow's the last."

The next evening, in the last half hour of free time, the streamer propped her phone in front of the old broom among the cleaning tools in the entrance hall and left for her shower. {WITCH_NAME} stayed silent out of frame, as always. Only she knew that a thing her Magic set talking would keep on after she walked away. She left the broom talking and walked out to the shower room. Under the running water, she twisted the streamer's towel around her throat from behind and pulled until she went still.

At lockup, the prisoners found the streamer dead in the shower room. She had never come back to sign off the show. In the trial court, everyone knew a thing talked only with {WITCH_NAME} beside it, and on the recorded show the broom never stopped talking, so they ruled her out.

Then one prisoner played the last show through the part nobody had listened to. "She's got up and gone," the broom said. "I'll keep on till she's back." The court understood: {WITCH_NAME} had left the broom talking to no one and gone to the shower room.
fields.epitaph: The only story anyone heard to the end was the one about her leaving.
fields.epithet: The Teller No One Hears Out
execution: The execution stand raises a giant iron notebook lying open. She is chained flat on its left page among engraved entries. She reads aloud the entry beside her face: where the old clock came from. Mid-sentence, the right half swings over on its spine and shuts on her. The notebook lies shut. No voice comes from between its pages.

magic.name: Things Talk Back
magic.text: Any object she speaks to answers in its own voice and tells her what it has been through.
